operations.title: Arithmetic divisibility and zero-one reduction for order 23
operations.summary: This program organizes exact arithmetic reductions for determinants of 23×23 sign matrices: the correspondence with 22×22 zero-one determinants, universal divisibility by 2^22 and its sharpness, divisibility rounding of the supplied real upper estimate, and exact replay of the arithmetic constants and determinant examples. These results certify D_23 ≤ 2^22·711,034,613 = 2,982,295,321,444,352. The program does not derive or improve the underlying analytic estimate and provides no exhaustive classification, endpoint-attainability proof, or restriction specific to near-maximal determinants.

operations.title: Order-23 sign/zero-one determinant correspondence
operations.summary: There is an exact correspondence D_23 = 2^22 max{|det B| : B is a 22×22 zero-one matrix}. Normalizing a 23×23 sign matrix and subtracting its first row gives |det A| = 2^22|det B|; conversely, A(B) = [[1,1^T],[1,J−2B]] satisfies det A(B) = (−2)^22 det B. Examples with B=0, B=I_22, and B=C⊕I_19 produce quotient values 0, 1, and −2, ruling out a nontrivial universal quotient residue class and exhibiting both parities among nonsingular examples. These examples do not exclude restrictions applying only near the maximum.

operations.title: Greatest universal divisor of order-23 sign determinants
operations.summary: Every 23×23 sign-matrix determinant, including zero, is divisible by 2^22. This follows from the normalized zero-one reduction |det A| = 2^22|det B|. The divisor is sharp: taking B=I_22 in the converse construction gives a sign matrix with determinant 2^22, so 2^22 is the greatest positive integer dividing all order-23 sign determinants. This does not establish attainability or sharpness of an upper bound and leaves open stronger restrictions specific to high-determinant matrices.

operations.title: Divisibility-rounded upper estimate for D_23
operations.summary: Using the supplied analytic estimate D_23 ≤ 2^22·31,640,625√505 and universal divisibility by 2^22, write D_23=2^22q with integer q. The exact floor is q ≤ floor(31,640,625√505)=711,034,613, giving D_23 ≤ 2,982,295,321,444,352. This endpoint is 186,421 below the ordinary integer floor of the real endpoint. It is the strongest rounding based solely on a common universal determinant divisor, but the result does not establish that quotient 711,034,613 occurs, that the endpoint is attainable, or that it equals D_23.

operations.title: Exact replay method for order-23 divisibility rounding
operations.summary: The supplied verifier is an independently replayable exact-arithmetic resource for the divisibility-rounding constants and determinant examples. It uses integer arithmetic and integer square root, checks the quotient and endpoint floors and rounded-endpoint multiplication, constructs sign matrices from B=I_22 and B=C⊕I_19, and evaluates their determinants by integer Bareiss elimination with exact-divisibility checks. It is not exhaustive, does not classify near-maximal determinants or establish endpoint attainability, and no execution transcript was supplied; the universal theorem rests on the accepted symbolic argument rather than computational enumeration.
